key_insight: The paper turns fault-tolerant stabilizer-state preparation into an integer linear program, automatically finding flag-based circuits with lower or equal gate count while detecting up to three errors.
engineering_relevance: This enables more efficient and reliable logical-state initialization and ancilla preparation for quantum error correction, reducing both circuit overhead and time-to-solution.
method: Formulate flag-circuit construction with the circuit gauge operator formalism.
Solve for optimized state-preparation and error-detecting circuits via integer linear programming.
Apply the method to derive a Steane-style error correction gadget for the [[24, 10, 4]] code.
evidence_signal: On Quantinuum H2, the derived gadget was tested with 10,000 shots and achieved a logical block error rate of about 0.00014 (about 0.000014 per logical qubit), with roughly 1.6% of shots post-selected due to weight-two errors.
watch_item: The demonstrated performance depends on post-selection and a specific hardware setting, so practical overhead and scalability may increase for larger codes or noisier devices.
paper_title: Automated Flag-based Fault-Tolerant State Preparation using Integer Linear Programming
